words.description: German scientist central to the Aether storyline. Ultimis Richtofen belongs to the original crew; his alternate incarnation belongs to Primis, introduced in Origins.
American Marine represented in the Ultimis and Primis crews. Introduced as a named character in Shi No Numa; later lore also places Ultimis Dempsey at Verrückt.
Russian soldier in the Ultimis and Primis crews. A central playable character throughout the Aether storyline.
Japanese soldier in the Ultimis and Primis crews, known for his devotion to honour and the Emperor.
Ludvig Maxis's daughter and a central Zombies character. She controls the undead during much of the early Aether storyline.
Group 935 scientist and Samantha's father. A major figure in the Aether storyline and rival to Richtofen.
Fictionalised version of the US president, playable in Black Ops's Pentagon-set Zombies map Five.
Nickname of Albert Arlington, one of the four Alcatraz inmates playable in Black Ops II's Mob of the Dead.
Alcatraz inmate nicknamed the Weasel, playable in Mob of the Dead. He designs the group's makeshift escape plane.
Playable member of Victis, the survivor crew from Black Ops II's TranZit, Die Rise and Buried.
Victis survivor who can hear Richtofen's instructions. Formerly associated with the zombie-flesh-eating group known as The Flesh.
Technically minded Victis survivor, playable in TranZit, Die Rise, Buried and Tag der Toten.
Victis survivor and former Broken Arrow operative, playable in Black Ops II and Tag der Toten.
Fictionalised film director who becomes the powerful, roaming zombie enemy in Call of the Dead.
Apothicon antagonist who manipulates the Shadows of Evil crew and returns in Revelations.
Powerful Keeper associated with Agartha and the House. Guides Primis while maintaining the repeating Aether cycle.
Requiem's field commander in Cold War Zombies and a member of the playable Ex-Requiem crew in Black Ops 6 and 7.
Dark Aether antagonist of Black Ops 7 who imprisons the Shadowsmiths and confronts the crew. Distinct from Alcatraz's Brutus.
Stuffed rabbit associated with the Mystery Box, secrets and encounters in the Dark Aether Zombies games.
Mob boss and Alcatraz inmate, playable as one of the four prisoners in Black Ops II's Mob of the Dead.
Violent Alcatraz inmate, playable in Mob of the Dead alongside Sal, Finn and the Weasel.
Alcatraz inmate nicknamed Finn, one of the four playable prisoners in Black Ops II's Mob of the Dead.
Fictionalised Richard Nixon, one of the four playable historical figures fighting zombies in the Pentagon on Five.
Fictionalised Cuban leader, playable alongside Kennedy, Nixon and McNamara on Black Ops's map Five.
Fictionalised US Secretary of Defense, one of the four playable characters in Black Ops's Five.
Actor appearing as a fictionalised version of himself in Black Ops's celebrity-cast Zombies map Call of the Dead.
Actress appearing as a fictionalised version of herself in Black Ops's Call of the Dead.
Actor appearing as a fictionalised version of himself in Black Ops's Call of the Dead.
Actor appearing as a fictionalised version of himself in Black Ops's Call of the Dead.
Boxer and one of the four playable characters in Black Ops III's Shadows of Evil.
Stage magician and one of the four playable characters in Shadows of Evil.
Burlesque performer and one of the four playable characters in Shadows of Evil.
Corrupt police detective and one of the four playable characters in Shadows of Evil.
Electrical humanoid enemy encountered in TranZit and Alpha Omega; linked to Broken Arrow's Cornelius Pernell.
Filipina smuggler searching for her brother Nathan. Joins the Ex-Requiem crew on Terminus in Black Ops 6.
Requiem scientist specialising in unnatural sciences, later a playable member of the Ex-Requiem crew.
US military officer who oversees Requiem's military operations, later a playable member of Ex-Requiem.
Leader of Black Ops 4's Chaos crew, searching for her father Alistair Rhodes.
Soviet operative who assists Requiem, introduced in Cold War's Firebase Z.
Scientist working with Omega Group in Cold War; later helps the imprisoned Requiem team escape from Terminus.
Maxis's assistant, later associated with the S.O.P.H.I.A. artificial-intelligence system encountered in Gorod Krovi.
Powerful Dark Aether entity revealed to be Kazimir Zykov, and the final boss of Cold War's Forsaken.
Soviet colonel and leader of Omega Group in the Cold War Zombies storyline.
Doctor Oskar Strauss, Requiem's head of energy research and a scientific adviser in the Dark Aether storyline.
Eccentric chemist and family friend of Scarlett Rhodes, playable as a member of Black Ops 4's Chaos crew.
Mexican adventurer and member of the playable Chaos crew in Black Ops 4.
French member of the playable Chaos crew in Black Ops 4, known for his strength and troubled past.
Omega scientist and Ulrich Vogel's daughter, transformed into the main boss of Cold War's Mauer der Toten.
Title used by Edward 'Eddie' Richtofen as the secretive head of Requiem and Project Janus in the Dark Aether storyline.
Black Ops 7 supernatural character released from the Seal of Sorrows in Ashes of the Damned.
Alistair Rhodes's butler and one of the four playable characters in Dead of the Night.
Stage-show gunslinger and one of the four playable guests defending Rhodes Manor in Dead of the Night.
Performer known as Madame Mirela, one of the four playable characters in Dead of the Night.
Brigadier General and one of the four playable guests at Rhodes Manor in Dead of the Night.
American intelligence operative who infiltrated Group 935. His story is associated with Shi No Numa and Alpha Omega.
Group 935 scientist who oversees Griffin Station on the Moon and communicates with Richtofen during Der Eisendrache.
Scarlett Rhodes's father, an explorer whose disappearance motivates the Chaos crew's search in Black Ops 4.
Maya's brother, subjected to experiments at Terminus and encountered as a mutated boss during its main quest.
Doctor Pericles Panos, the Project Janus scientist who directs players through the Liberty Falls main quest.
Richtofen's Mexican test subject, later encountered as the Hermit helping Victis in Tag der Toten.
Soviet soldier trapped in the Dark Aether who communicates as the Stranger and is revealed to be the Forsaken.
Winged horse appearing in Ancient Evil, used for transport and associated with the Pegasus Strike equipment.
Shadowsmith and main-quest boss of Black Ops 7's Ashes of the Damned.
Shadowsmith also called the Needle, confronted as the main-quest boss of Black Ops 7's Astra Malorum.
Shadowsmith also called the Forge, confronted as the main-quest boss of Black Ops 7's Totenreich.
Shadowsmith also called the Warp, confronted as the main-quest boss of Black Ops 7's Kowakujō.
John Blanchard, Project Janus's security chief who guides the response to Liberty Falls.
Leader of Broken Arrow who becomes the electrical entity known as the Avogadro, central to Alpha Omega.
Former Ascension Group scientist who becomes the Pentagon Thief encountered on Five.
Scientist in charge of Projekt Endstation, whose work opened a gateway to the Dark Aether beneath Die Maschine.
Blacksmith associated with the creation of Pack-a-Punch. His history is revealed through Tag der Toten's audio recordings.
Doctor Revati Modi, the scientist responsible for the human experiments conducted at the Terminus research facility.
Group 935 scientist involved in Richtofen's early teleportation experiments and the establishment of Griffin Station.
Aggressive undead dogs, first encountered in World at War's Shi No Numa in 2009. Their original Aether backstory is linked to Samantha's dog Fluffy.
Heavily armoured enemy introduced in Origins, attacking with a flamethrower and mechanical claw.
Armoured Alcatraz guard enemy in Mob of the Dead and Blood of the Dead, able to disable interactive objects.
Armoured zombie soldier with an arm-mounted cannon, introduced in Gorod Krovi and recurring in later Zombies games.
Large, three-headed Apothicon enemy introduced in Shadows of Evil. Its glowing open mouths are weak points.
Small, crawling mutant that releases a disorienting gas cloud when killed; familiar from Kino der Toten and Five.
Weapon-stealing enemy encountered during special rounds on Five; revealed to be Yuri Zavoyski.
Small creature that jumps onto players' heads in TranZit's fog and can interact with green streetlights to create portals.
Ascension special-round enemy that attacks perk machines and can steal players' purchased perks.
Radioactive elite enemy introduced in Die Maschine, splitting into two smaller enemies after its initial defeat.
Large three-headed enemy introduced in Forsaken, attacking with a charge and electrical beams from its mouths.
Toxic undead dog introduced in Die Maschine, leaving a damaging gas cloud after death.
Burning zombie introduced in Shangri-La, exploding when approached and leaving a dangerous fire patch.
Fast, pale Shangri-La zombie whose scream temporarily blinds or disorients nearby players.
Floating enemy introduced in Mauer der Toten that empowers nearby zombies and drains players' health.
Supernatural being from the Aether storyline. Hostile Keepers appear during encounters such as Shadows of Evil's rituals.
Large plant-infested enemy from Zetsubou No Shima, with vulnerable orange growths and the ability to swallow downed players.
Flying creature introduced in Shadows of Evil, attacking players with projectiles and returning in later Zombies games.
Zombie protected by armour, requiring players to break or bypass its protection before dealing full damage to covered areas.
Spider-like enemy introduced in Black Ops 6, rushing and leaping at players during special rounds and mixed waves.
Large mass of fused human bodies, introduced in Black Ops 6. Can grab and pull players toward itself.
Armoured ancient warrior encountered in Origins; special waves attack the generators and try to shut them down.
Large, mutated enemy in Black Ops 4's Chaos maps that can grab players with its tongue and obstruct purchasable objects.
Fast, two-headed special enemy introduced on Citadelle des Morts in Black Ops 6.
Flying electrical drone from Gorod Krovi, attacking with beams and capable of electrifying nearby zombies.
Armoured arena enemy from IX, using heavy melee attacks and throwable weapons.
Large wolf-like enemy from Dead of the Night; silver bullets are especially effective against it.
Heavy Voyage of Despair enemy associated with the Titanic's boiler rooms, attacking with a shovel and burning projectiles.
Electrically charged Mimic variant introduced in Black Ops 6's The Tomb. Disguises itself as loot, grabs players with its tendrils and causes visual and radar disruption.
Teleporting electrical enemy from Cold War, attacking at range and capable of disabling vehicles in Outbreak.
Elemental zombie from Black Ops 4's Chaos maps, with fire, water, electrical and poison/decay variants.
Radioactive canine enemy introduced in Black Ops 7's Paradox Junction, rushing players and exploding.
Fast, four-legged pack hunter from Black Ops 7, found in Ashes of the Damned and Survival maps. Can consume dropped items.
Explosive, toxin-associated zombie introduced in Black Ops 6's Shattered Veil and returning on later maps.
Burning zombie variant encountered in Black Ops 7's Kowakujō, closely related to the Napalm Zombie.
Multi-armed giant from Ancient Evil, carrying weapons and a shield and attacking at both close and long range.
Elite Disciple variant introduced in Black Ops 6's Shattered Veil, able to force other enemies to evolve into stronger forms.
Undead Viking warrior from Totenreich, wielding a trident and a large mutated crab claw.
Large spider-like elite enemy from Rex Infernus, using webbing to slow players and cocoon zombies.
Fast, spider-like enemies from Rex Infernus that attack in groups and can fire slowing web projectiles.
Energy-pistol Wonder Weapon that fires explosive green projectiles. Its Zombies debut was World at War's Nacht der Untoten.
Wonder Weapon that releases a powerful blast of compressed air, throwing zombies away. Introduced on Kino der Toten in Black Ops.
Electrical Wonder Weapon that chains lightning through groups of zombies. Introduced on World at War's Shi No Numa.
Three-round-burst Ray Gun successor introduced in Black Ops II. Its penetrating energy shots can hit multiple zombies.
Dual-wielded, explosive-firing Pack-a-Punch upgrade of the M1911. Introduced in Black Ops in 2010, not World at War.
Purchasable melee knife that replaces the standard knife attack; introduced in World at War's Der Riese.
Double-barrelled shotgun familiar as an early-round wall weapon in Black Ops and Black Ops II. Returns as an Ultra-rarity legacy weapon in Black Ops 7's Rex Infernus.
Four-barrelled shotgun Wonder Weapon introduced in Mob of the Dead, returning in Blood of the Dead and Black Ops 7's Paradox Junction.
Tentacled Wonder Weapon from Shadows of Evil that fires projectiles creating temporary black holes which consume enemies.
Ice-element Wonder Weapon introduced in Origins, where it upgrades to Ull's Arrow. A reworked version returns in Black Ops 6's The Tomb.
Buildable fire-element staff from Origins. Its upgraded form is Kagutsuchi's Blood.
Buildable lightning-element staff from Origins. Its upgraded form is Kimat's Bite.
Buildable wind-element staff from Origins. Its upgraded form is Boreas' Fury.
Common name for the lightning-upgraded bow in Der Eisendrache, whose charged arrows create electrical storms.
Fan name for the Thrustodyne Aeronautics Model 23, a turbine-based Wonder Weapon featured in TranZit and Liberty Falls.
Die Rise Wonder Weapon that fires slippery purple liquid, allowing kills to spread between nearby zombies.
Bow Wonder Weapon earned by feeding the three stone dragons in Der Eisendrache; can be upgraded into four elemental bows.
Buried Wonder Weapon that slows and destroys enemies with an energy beam and can lift its user into the air.
Common name for Gorod Krovi's dual-wielded GKZ-45 Mk3 Wonder Weapon; the paired guns combine their shots to create a black hole.
Moon Wonder Weapon formed by combining two Zap Guns; its microwave-like blast causes zombies to inflate and explode.
Freeze-based Wonder Weapon introduced on Five, with a later version appearing in Classified.
Explosive sniper-rifle Wonder Weapon introduced in Call of the Dead.
Weapon with a launchable knife blade. Its Pack-a-Punched version can revive teammates when its blade hits them.
World War II-era submachine gun available in World at War Zombies.
Pump-action grenade launcher appearing in Black Ops Zombies.
Flame-projecting weapon available in World at War Zombies, used to burn enemies.
Wolf-themed upgraded bow in Der Eisendrache, firing spectral attacks that knock down groups of enemies.
Void-themed upgraded bow in Der Eisendrache, using a vortex and spectral skulls to attack enemies.
Fire-themed upgraded bow in Der Eisendrache, using burning attacks and explosive charged shots.
Acid-converted Blundergat firing sticky, delayed-explosion projectiles. In Mob of the Dead, the Pack-a-Punched Vitriolic Withering adds the zombie-attracting effect.
Fire-converted Blundergat created through a quest in Blood of the Dead.
Pack-a-Punch name of the Thundergun, with improved ammunition capacity.
Base D.I.E. Wonder Weapon from Die Maschine, combining a powerful shockwave shot with a suction mode used to replenish ammunition.
Terminus Wonder Weapon with a slowing beam and an energy attack that damages affected enemies.
Forsaken Wonder Weapon with two forms: a crystalline melee axe and an energy-firing gun.
Powerful melee weapon earned through a hidden quest in Mob of the Dead, with a related version in Blood of the Dead.
Buildable specialist sword in Shadows of Evil, with an upgraded form called the Keeper Sword.
Zetsubou No Shima specialist weapon that uses supernatural power to mesmerise or vaporise enemies.
Gorod Krovi specialist weapon combining a flamethrower gauntlet with a deployable baby dragon.
Base sword obtained in Citadelle des Morts, which can be transformed into one of four elemental Wonder Weapons.
Tentacled, cannon-like Wonder Weapon from Voyage of Despair that can receive elemental upgrades.
IX Wonder Weapon shaped like a scorpion, capable of firing shots that hold and damage enemies.
Dead of the Night Wonder Weapon found in Alistair Rhodes's mansion and upgraded through Chaos Theory into Alistair's Annihilator.
Ice-based Wonder Weapon from Tag der Toten, visually related to the Thundergun but firing freezing projectiles.
Black Ops 4 Chaos specialist weapon: an electrically charged hammer that gains additional abilities as it levels.
Black Ops 4 Chaos specialist weapon: a staff whose beam can damage enemies and help revive teammates.
Black Ops 4 Chaos specialist weapon combining a melee sword with a powerful pistol.
Black Ops 4 Chaos specialist weapon consisting of throwable bladed rings that return to their wielder.
Charon-associated Wonder Weapon from Ancient Evil, one of four elemental hands that can be awakened and further upgraded.
Gaia-associated Wonder Weapon from Ancient Evil, using earth-related attacks against enemies.
Hemera-associated Wonder Weapon from Ancient Evil, using light-related attacks against enemies.
Ouranos-associated Wonder Weapon from Ancient Evil, using wind-related attacks against enemies.
Secret crossbow Wonder Weapon acquired through a side quest in Dead of the Night.
Organic Wonder Weapon from Black Ops 6's Reckoning, developed by Doctor Panos using Dark Aether power.
Living Wonder Weapon from Black Ops 7's Ashes of the Damned. Fires liquid spikes which impale enemies and can be recalled for further damage.
Fire-wielding melee Wonder Weapon introduced with Black Ops 7's Totenreich.
Cat-spirit Wonder Weapon from Black Ops 7's Kowakujō. Attacks with spirit bolts, corrosive hairballs and a scratching melee strike.
Dual-crossbow Wonder Weapon from Black Ops 7's Rex Infernus, used against the Warden and his summoned Dread Skulls.
Upgraded Blundergat variant from Black Ops 7's Paradox Junction, with soul-based attacks and a focused energy beam.
CRBR-S conversion kit variant from Mauer der Toten, firing a concentrated energy beam.
CRBR-S conversion kit variant from Mauer der Toten, firing explosive, lock-on projectiles.
CRBR-S conversion kit variant from Mauer der Toten, firing a spread of energy projectiles like a shotgun.
Bolt-action rifle available in World at War's Nacht der Untoten.
Black Ops Zombies map set in an abandoned German theatre, featuring the Thundergun, teleportation and Nova Crawlers.
The original Zombies map, released with World at War in 2008. Players defend a small, ruined building near an airfield.
World at War map set in Group 935's research facility. Introduced the Pack-a-Punch machine and linked teleporters.
Black Ops II experience set across Green Run, with a bus connecting locations through fog and lava.
Black Ops II map set at a World War I excavation site in France, introducing Primis, giant robots and elemental staffs.
Black Ops II map set in a supernatural version of Alcatraz, following four prisoners trapped in a repeating cycle.
Black Ops III launch map set in Morg City, featuring four new characters, Beast Mode and the Apothicon Servant.
Black Ops III map set in an Austrian castle, featuring the Wrath of the Ancients and four upgraded bows.
Black Ops II map set in an underground Western town, featuring Arthur, the Paralyzer and a haunted mansion.
Black Ops II Zombies version of the Nuketown nuclear-test site, with perks and Pack-a-Punch arriving during the match.
Black Ops map set at a Soviet launch facility, introducing lunar landers, Gersh Devices and perk-stealing Space Monkeys.
World at War swamp map, introducing the playable original four-character crew, Hellhounds and the Wunderwaffe DG-2.
World at War map set in a German asylum. Introduced purchasable perks and electrical traps to Zombies.
Black Ops III reimagining of Der Riese, retaining its factory layout, teleporters and Pack-a-Punch.
Black Ops map set at a frozen Siberian outpost, featuring a celebrity cast and George Romero as a roaming enemy.
Black Ops III map set in a devastated Stalingrad, featuring dragons, Manglers and the GKZ-45 Mk3.
Final Black Ops III Zombies map, combining fragments of earlier locations around Agartha and the House.
Black Ops II map set across damaged skyscrapers in Shanghai, featuring elevators, the Trample Steam and the Sliquifier.
Black Ops jungle-temple map featuring traps, a time-travel quest and the shrink-ray Wonder Weapon.
Black Ops 6 map set in a West Virginia town overrun by a Dark Aether outbreak, connected to Project Janus.
Cold War launch map set around the ruined Nacht der Untoten building and an underground Projekt Endstation facility.
Black Ops 6 map set at an island prison and research facility in the Philippine Sea, featuring the Beamsmasher.
Black Ops 4 expansion of Alcatraz with Primis as the playable crew, featuring the Spectral Shield and Magmagat.
Black Ops III map set on a Pacific island used for biological experiments, featuring Thrashers and the KT-4.
Cold War map set at an Omega Group outpost in Vietnam, featuring Mimics, Manglers and the RAI K-84.
Cold War map set in divided Berlin, featuring Klaus, the CRBR-S and a confrontation with Valentina.
Black Ops 4 reimagining of Five, set in the Pentagon with access to Groom Lake.
Black Ops 4 Chaos map aboard the Titanic, featuring the Sentinel Artifact and Kraken Wonder Weapon.
Black Ops 6 map set in an Avalon village and castle, featuring four elemental sword Wonder Weapons.
Black Ops 4 Chaos map set in the hidden city of Delphi, featuring Pegasus and four elemental hand weapons.
Black Ops 4 Chaos map set at Rhodes Manor, featuring a guest cast, vampires, werewolves and Alistair's Folly.
Final Black Ops 4 Aether map, returning Victis to the Siberian outpost in a reimagining of Call of the Dead.
Black Ops 4 map expanding the Nuketown setting with a Broken Arrow facility, Rushmore and upgraded Ray Gun Mark II variants.
Final Cold War round-based map, set at an Omega test facility and concluding with the battle against the Forsaken.
Black Ops 7 launch map connecting locations displaced into the Dark Aether, featuring Ol' Tessie and the Necrofluid Gauntlet.
Black Ops 6 map set beneath an excavation site, with ancient catacombs, a Dark Aether Nexus and the returning Staff of Ice.
Black Ops 6 map set at Colton Hall near Liberty Falls, featuring Elder Disciples and new Ray Gun Mark II variants.
Final Black Ops 6 Zombies map, set in Project Janus's headquarters and featuring the Gorgofex Wonder Weapon.
Black Ops 7 map set at a remote observatory, with a main quest leading to a confrontation with the Shadowsmith Caltheris.
Black Ops 7 map set in a time-distorted version of Nuketown, featuring Rad-Hounds and the returning Blundergat.
Black Ops 7 map set in the Norwegian village of Eidskallen, featuring Necropincers and the Jotunn Star.
Black Ops 7 map set around a Japanese castle in a volcanic landscape, featuring the Nekomancer and Shadowsmith Nyxara.
Black Ops 7 map set in the Warden's Dark Aether domain, featuring Deathspinners, the Web Mother and Warden's Blight.
San Francisco prison island used as the setting for Mob of the Dead and Blood of the Dead.
US Department of Defense headquarters, used as the Zombies setting for Five and Classified.
Black Ops II Zombies location containing TranZit's interconnected bus route and the Bus Depot, Farm and Town survival areas.
San Francisco bridge reached by the escape plane in Mob of the Dead, where Pack-a-Punch is located.
Otherworldly area in Origins reached through elemental portals. Contains the staff crystals and upgrade pedestals; the base staffs are assembled beneath the Excavation Site.
Area 51 location in Nevada, visited at the start of Moon and accessible in Classified.
Fictional city that forms the setting of Black Ops III's Shadows of Evil.
Central dig-site area in Origins, containing the underground chamber where the elemental staffs are assembled.
Haunted mansion in Buried, occupied by ghostly women whose attacks steal players' points.
Common name for Der Eisendrache's undercroft, containing the pyramid and its low-gravity mechanism.
The abandoned asylum setting associated with Verrückt; Asylum is also the name of its related World at War multiplayer map.
The House in Agartha associated with Doctor Monty, the children and the events of Revelations.
Remote island complex in the Philippine Sea containing the prison and research facilities explored in Terminus.
Bowling alley in Liberty Falls, associated with its bowling side quest.
General description of the Soviet rocket-launch facility that forms Ascension's setting.
Codename associated with the Der Eisendrache castle and Group 935's operations there.
Shadows of Evil district containing the theatre used for Jessica Rose's ritual.
Shadows of Evil district containing the boxing gym used for Floyd Campbell's ritual.
Shadows of Evil district containing the Ruby Rabbit and Jack Vincent's ritual.
Building in Shadows of Evil's Canal District used for Jack Vincent's ritual.
Central junction in Shadows of Evil, connecting the main routes into Morg City's districts.
Research installation belonging to Broken Arrow; the Nuketown site and its underground facilities are explored in Alpha Omega.
Snow-covered lake area within Ashes of the Damned, one of the locations displaced into the Dark Aether.
One of IX's four deity-themed towers, with an altar room and underground connections.
One of IX's four deity-themed towers, dedicated to Zeus.
One of IX's four deity-themed towers, dedicated to Ra and involved in its main quest.
One of IX's four deity-themed towers, dedicated to Danu and involved in its main quest.
Three-tower Project Janus headquarters near Liberty Falls; the setting of Black Ops 6's Reckoning.
Town area within Ashes of the Damned, also released as a standalone Black Ops 7 Survival map.
Farm area within Ashes of the Damned, also available as a standalone Black Ops 7 Survival map.
Soviet-era launch-site area within Ashes of the Damned, also available as a standalone Black Ops 7 Survival map.
Otherworldly area reached through portals in The Tomb, involved in its Staff of Ice and main-quest progression.
Lighthouse section of Totenreich's Eidskallen setting, also released as a Black Ops 7 Survival map.
Perk that increases maximum health, allowing the player to survive more hits. One of the original perks introduced in Verrückt.
Perk that speeds up teammate revives. Its solo and health-regeneration benefits vary between Zombies games.
Perk chiefly associated with faster reloading; additional handling benefits vary by game.
The original Double Tap perk increases weapon firing speed. Introduced with World at War's Verrückt.
Movement perk that improves sprinting, with its precise speed and stamina benefits varying by game.
Perk allowing the player to carry a third weapon. Introduced in Black Ops's Moon.
Perk associated with protection from self-inflicted explosive damage and explosive dive-to-prone attacks. Introduced in Ascension.
Reworked Double Tap introduced in Black Ops II, increasing firing speed and making bullet weapons fire two projectiles per round consumed.
Accuracy and headshot-focused perk, including head-targeting aim assistance on supported control schemes.
Web-themed perk introduced in Shadows of Evil. Black Ops III uses web grenades and defensive webs; Black Ops 7 triggers a web explosion when melee damage leaves health low.
Perk introduced in Mob of the Dead that releases an electrical discharge when the player reloads.
Loot-focused perk introduced in Buried. Modern versions increase useful drops; Black Ops 7 Season 06 also lets its ammo pickups partially replenish alternate weapon ammunition.
Death-recovery perk introduced in Black Ops II. Its tombstone and shadow-form mechanics differ between versions.
Cold War perk that gives attacks a chance to trigger random Ammo Mod effects.
Sliding-based explosive perk in Black Ops 4 and Cold War, with explosive protection varying by upgrade level. In Black Ops 6 and 7, PhD Slider is a PhD Flopper Augment.
Die Rise perk that creates a playable doppelganger when the player goes down, allowing an attempt to revive the original body.
Perk that improves awareness by revealing enemies through obstacles; additional benefits vary by game.
Black Ops 6 perk that replaces a weapon-butt attack with a powerful punch and boosts melee effectiveness.
Black Ops 4 perk that prevents a lethal hit from immediately downing the player, instead triggering a temporary invulnerable Berserk state.
Black Ops 4 defensive perk that releases freezing blasts when triggered by enemy hits, subject to available charges.
Black Ops 4 perk that reduces equipment, trap and fast-travel cooldowns and speeds up Mystery Box and Pack-a-Punch processing.
Black Ops 4 perk that makes a held shield protect from every direction and causes an explosion when the shield breaks.
Black Ops 4 perk that creates a defensive circle while the player stays in place, building damage and armour bonuses.
Black Ops 4 perk slot that grants a random perk not assigned to another slot; buying it again changes the selection.
Black Ops 4 perk that increases the ammunition a player can carry in reserve.
Black Ops 4 perk that releases a damaging electrical discharge on reload, with stronger effects from a more depleted magazine.
Black Ops 4 accuracy perk with head-targeting aim assistance, reduced hip-fire spread and reduced recoil.
Black Ops 4 perk that improves offhand melee attacks, allowing swipes to hit multiple enemies and restore a little health.
Black Ops 4 perk that can summon the spectral wolf Luna to attack enemies after the player deals sufficient damage.
Black Ops 7 perk that periodically summons a spectral Wisp ally after sustained combat; Augments can change its role.
Black Ops 4 perk that can make killed zombies leave contamination fields which slow enemies and increase damage against them.
Black Ops 4 perk that charges while crouching, then sends the player dashing through enemies in a burst of fire.
Wind-up monkey-shaped explosive that attracts nearby zombies before detonating. Introduced in World at War's Der Riese.
Timed fragmentation grenade used to damage enemies with an explosion; can be cooked before throwing.
Sticky explosive grenade that attaches to surfaces or enemies before detonating.
Placeable directional explosive mine, familiar from Black Ops Zombies.
Buildable defensive shield that blocks attacks in the direction it covers; several maps feature their own variants.
Returning throwable tomahawk earned by feeding the three hellhounds in Mob of the Dead.
Throwable device that creates a black hole, killing nearby zombies and allowing players to teleport through it.
Small creature thrown in a jar to distract and attack zombies, introduced in Shadows of Evil.
Shortened label for the Quantum Entanglement Device from Moon, a throwable device producing unpredictable effects.
Buried equipment that records a point in the match and can rewind players and the game state to it.
Russian nesting-doll explosive from Ascension, releasing multiple smaller explosive dolls.
Origins equipment that marks a target area for bombardment by the giant robots.
Buildable drone in Origins that carries Maxis's brain and assists players with attacks, revives and quest tasks.
Consumable equipment allowing the player to revive themselves after being downed without a teammate's help.
Armour-restoration pickups used to replace missing plates in the player's equipped armour.
Thrown bottle that creates a burning patch on impact, damaging enemies passing through it.
Throwable device that uses sound to draw the attention of nearby ordinary zombies.
Throwable axe used for direct-hit kills and recoverable for reuse in supported versions.
Consumable tactical equipment that rapidly restores the player's health when used.
Deployable electrical tactical equipment that stuns or immobilises affected enemies.
Throwable grenade that creates a temporary cloud of smoke, obscuring sight.
Moon device used to hack objects and shut down excavators; holding it prevents simultaneous use of the P.E.S.
Upgraded shovel earned through digging in Origins, improving the rewards and opportunities from dig sites.
The Pressurised External Suit helmet on Moon, allowing the player to breathe in areas without oxygen.
Black Ops 4 throwable equipment that creates blue flames which burn enemies.
Tag der Toten throwable that distracts zombies with a music box and Samantha-like figure before detonating.
Body armour equipment that increases the player's protection; capacity and mechanics vary by game.
Special armour that regenerates automatically over time. In Black Ops 6, it can be earned through The Tomb's Golden Armor side quest.
Upgrade item that raises a weapon's rarity tier, increasing its damage.
